Extract posterior draws from fitted mvgam objects

Source: R/as.data.frame.mvgam.R
mvgam_draws.Rd

Extract posterior draws as a data frame, matrix or array, or as one of the posterior::draws_* classes. Parameters take their brms names, such as b_x and sd_grp__Intercept. A trend parameter indexed by series takes the series name, as in sigma_trend[series_1]. The integrated data model article contrasts intercepts drawn with as_draws_df().

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = TRUE,
  variable = NULL,
  draw = NULL,
  regex = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam
as.matrix(x, variable = NULL, draw = NULL, regex = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as.array(x, variable = NULL, draw = NULL, regex = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws_matrix(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws_df(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws_array(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws_list(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
as_draws_rvars(x, variable = NULL, regex = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object.

row.names, optional

Ignored.

variable

Either a keyword shortcut, a character vector of parameter names, or (when regex = TRUE) a vector of regular expressions. Recognised keywords:

  • "betas": population-level coefficients, the set brms::fixef() reports (b_*, bs_* and bsp_*).

  • "obs_params": observation-family distributional parameters (sigma, phi, shape, ...).

  • "smooth_params": smooth-term standard deviations (sds_*).

  • "trend_betas": the trend formula's population-level coefficients (b_*_trend, bs_*_trend and bsp_*_trend).

  • "trend_params": trend-dynamics parameters (autoregressive coefficients, innovation SDs, ...).

  • "trend_smooth_params": trend-side smooth SDs.

NULL (the default) returns every parameter. A bare vector name, such as "sigma_trend", selects every element. Group-level effects, factor loadings and latent states have no keyword. Select them by name. variables.mvgam() lists the names a fit holds.

draw

Optional positive integer indices of the draws to keep, counted across chains. NULL (the default) keeps every draw.

regex

Logical. When TRUE, each entry of variable is treated as a regular expression and any parameter matching at least one pattern is selected. Keyword shortcuts are still honoured. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

inc_warmup

Logical. Include warmup draws? Defaults to FALSE. A fit holds them only when sampled with save_warmup = TRUE.

Value

A data.frame, matrix, array, or one of the posterior::draws_* classes (draws_matrix, draws_array, draws_df, draws_list, draws_rvars) depending on the method dispatched.

See also

mvgam_diagnostics for higher-level summaries derived from these draws (rhat, neff_ratio, fixef, bayes_R2, posterior_summary, ...), variables.mvgam() to list every parameter name in the fit, mcmc_plot.mvgam() for diagnostic visualisations, summary.mvgam() for a printed model summary, tidy.mvgam() for a tibble of parameter summaries, posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam() for prediction-scale outputs, posterior::draws for the underlying draws classes.

Other posterior summaries: VarCorr.mvgam(), bibtex(), how_to_cite.mvgam(), hypothesis.mvgam(), index-mvgam, mcmc_plot.mvgam(), methods_md(), pairs.mvgam(), posterior_interval.mvgam(), ranef.mvgam(), smooths.mvgam(), summary.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Trend-dynamics parameters as a data frame of draws
head(as.data.frame(mod, variable = "trend_params"))
#>   sigma_trend[series_1] ar1_trend[series_1] .chain .iteration .draw
#> 1             0.4111121           0.4148928      1          1     1
#> 2             0.4219180           0.5387783      1          2     2
#> 3             0.3199136           0.7333736      1          3     3
#> 4             0.4825790           0.7190115      1          4     4
#> 5             0.4319198           0.7813397      1          5     5
#> 6             0.4639083           0.7478594      1          6     6

# Regular expressions select by pattern, here the smooth's basis
# coefficients and its smoothing SD
colnames(as.matrix(mod, variable = c("^s_", "^sds_"), regex = TRUE))
#> [1] "s_sx_1[1]" "s_sx_1[2]" "s_sx_1[3]" "s_sx_1[4]" "s_sx_1[5]" "s_sx_1[6]"
#> [7] "s_sx_1[7]" "s_sx_1[8]" "sds_sx_1" 

# One random variable per parameter, printed as mean and SD
as_draws_rvars(mod, variable = "trend_params")
#> # A draws_rvars: 1000 iterations, 2 chains, and 2 variables
#> $sigma_trend: rvar<1000,2>[1] mean ± sd:
#>      series_1 
#> 0.44 ± 0.073  
#> 
#> $ar1_trend: rvar<1000,2>[1] mean ± sd:
#>     series_1 
#> 0.59 ± 0.15  
#> 

# Next, mcmc_plot(mod) plots the same draws
# }
